summary: CASE picks a value based on conditions, like an if/else inside a query. Use it to label, group, or convert values.
notes: CASE checks each WHEN in order and uses the first one that is true, so WHEN grade >= 80 only sees grades under 90.
CASE grade_level WHEN 9 THEN ... compares one column to each value. CASE WHEN ... allows any condition.
Without ELSE, a row that matches no WHEN gets NULL.
pitfall: NULL fails every comparison, so a NULL grade skips all the WHEN grade >= ... lines and gets the ELSE value 'F'. Put WHEN grade IS NULL first.
